description: Run structured program/argv with the platform-native toolchain under the OS sandbox. File tools and commands use the same checkout. Plan commands may write when approved. Full access is unsandboxed; Benchmark keeps its offline worker. Runtime manages timeout and process-tree cleanup.

propertyDescriptions.executionScope: Default workspace sandbox. Request host for exact per-command host escalation; the approval includes full host filesystem and network access. Benchmark always remains container-confined.
propertyDescriptions.requiredCapabilities: Compatibility requirements only, never permission grants. test/verify assumes loopback_tcp for runtime IPC. Set [] for checks known not to need IPC. Missing capabilities can request a separately approved host invocation; Benchmark cannot escape. Do not patch language runtimes or repackage a denied command.
propertyDescriptions.program: Executable name or container Linux path for workspace commands (python3, node, bash). Dependencies are installed inside the task container. Never pass host Windows executable paths unless requesting separately approved host scope.
propertyDescriptions.args: Literal structured argv, including multiline code and punctuation. Supply real arguments, not an extra launcher name. For cmd /c pass the whole command as ONE argument, e.g. ["/c","dir /b"]. Prefer search_files mode=list for directory listing.
propertyDescriptions.cwd: Normal CLI workspace: /workspace or a relative directory; other Linux container directories are allowed. Host scope/Full access uses host paths. Benchmark resolves paths in its own worker. Arguments are literal and are never path-rewritten.
propertyDescriptions.intent: Declared purpose, not permission or proof of read-only behavior. Use test, build or verify for validation.
propertyDescriptions.verificationKind: Optional validation category: unit_test, integration_test, build, typecheck, lint, format_check, smoke_test, benchmark, custom. Missing verify/test categories default to custom; build defaults to build. Invalid or inapplicable metadata is normalized without blocking execution.
propertyDescriptions.timeoutMs: An optional requested command-phase timeout. Runtime applies the minimum of this request, the configured command limit, and the classified capability limit, then returns all four timeout values including the effective limit.
propertyDescriptions.reason: A concise explanation of why this command is needed for the current task.

guidance: Prefer direct test runners and existing scripts; Runtime compacts display output, so avoid piping test output through grep just to save tokens. Multiline Python -c/Node -e, shell scripts, heredocs, pipes, redirects and synchronous nested calls are supported. Use start_command with backgroundKind=service for persistent dev/API servers, then check readiness with a bounded TCP or HTTP probe before running a dependent smoke test; cancel and observe the service afterward. A timed-out foreground server was stopped: a later connection refusal does not prove sandbox network isolation. Use the default backgroundKind=job for finite long work. Bounded sleeps and timeout wrappers are allowed. Exit code and validation verdict are separate: an outer exit 0 does not prove tests passed. Unknown validation means insufficient evidence, not an instruction to rerun blindly. Command syntax is not a permission boundary. A known sandbox_boundary_violation is different from unknown execution: first adjust paths/cache/temp settings; a repeated incident in the same task, cwd and access class requires user approval. Approval never replays the stopped command. Changing argv or wrapping/obfuscating a denied operation does not reset that incident. Benchmark approval remains inside its task container. Background descendants are terminated when their command finishes; use start_command/poll_command to supervise long work. Never bypass network authorization, Benchmark isolation or sandbox failures; do not retry unknown execution or cleanup.
